title: Analysis of Cell Migration within a Three-dimensional Collagen Matrix
protocol: Mix paraffin wax and petroleum jelly in a 1:1 ratio.
Heat the mixture until it has melted.
Draw 2-3 layers of the paraffin wax/petroleum jelly mix on a glass slide according to specified dimensions.
Apply the heated paraffin wax/petroleum jelly mix rapidly to avoid solidification while drawing.
Add a coverslip to the solidified paraffin wax/petroleum jelly layer and seal it with 2-3 layers of paraffin wax/petroleum jelly mixture.
Place migration chambers in an upright position in a rack for the experiment.
Harvest cells, such as using 0.25% Trypsin/EDTA.
Count harvested cells.
Resuspend counted cells in complete media containing FCS, antibiotics, and recommended supplements.
Prepare 4-8 reaction tubes with 20 µl of cell suspension containing 4-6 x 10^4 cells.
Fill up to 50 µl with complete media for each tube.
Add 50 μl 10x MEM (pH 5.1-5.5) and 27 μl of 7.5% sodium bicarbonate solution (pH 9.0-9.5) to a reaction tube.
Mix thoroughly until the solution color turns from yellow-orange to intense purple.
Add 375 μl liquid collagen suspension to the mixture in the reaction tube.
Mix thoroughly until the pH of the final collagen suspension is about 7.5, indicated by a light purple color.
Add 100 µl of the final collagen suspension to 50 µl cell suspension and mix thoroughly.
Transfer 100 µl of the mixed collagen-cell suspension once up and down before use.
Combine the collagen-cell suspension with 10x MEM/sodium bicarbonate solution when pH value changes to 7.5.
Transfer the final collagen suspension cell mix from reaction tubes to migration chambers.
Gently tap migration chambers to distribute collagen suspension cell mix evenly on bottom.
Incubate migration chambers upright in a rack at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for about 30 min to allow polymerization of collagen fibers.
Switch on the microscope and the microscope stage heater.
Adjust the temperature to 37 °C.
Place migration chamber under a microscope.
Focus approximately 50 cells or more in the field of view using a 10X objective.
Record cell migration in time-lapse mode using a multi-camera video surveillance software application.
Save cell migration movies in an appropriate format, e.g., “*.avi” or “*.mov”.
Analyze cell migration movies using an appropriate cell tracking software application.
Randomly select at least 30 cells per experiment without prior knowledge of migratory activity.
Track the paths of selected cells by following the moving cells accurately with the mouse cursor positioned to the nucleus.
Determine xy-coordinates for lymphocytes/HSPCs every 0.75 seconds.
Determine xy-coordinates for tumor cells every 0.5 seconds.
Determine a total of 60 xy-coordinates per cell for a typical cell migration experiment.
Analyze cell tracking data by using an appropriate software application.
Copy the cell tracking raw data into a self-designed spreadsheet template.
Multiply the sum of numerical values representing total distance with a correction factor to convert pixels into micrometers.
Determine locomotory activity as a cell migration parameter.
Determine time of active movement as a cell migration parameter.
Identify cells that have migrated less than 25 µm as non-moving cells.
Replace numerical values of non-moving cells with commas.
Calculate statistical significance of the mean locomotory activity using the Mann-Whitney U test.
Consider a p-value < 0.05 as significant.
Display the mean locomotory activity of cells as an xy-diagram, BoxPlot diagram, or bar chart diagram.
Display single cell-based data such as time of active movement or speed as a bar chart diagram or histogram.
